canonical_question: Why was the wear test conducted at 300 °C specifically, and does this temperature exceed any phase stability limits for the CuMoTaWV equimolar system?

question_variants.question: Why was the wear test conducted at 300 °C specifically, and does this temperature exceed any phase stability limits for the CuMoTaWV equimolar system?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper reports wear tests at 300 °C and notes a higher coefficient of friction attributed to tribochemical reactions. It does not state why 300 °C was specifically chosen over other temperatures, nor does it provide phase stability data to confirm if 300 °C exceeds any stability limits for the CuMoTaWV system.

answers.answer: The wear test at 300 °C showed a high COF due to a tribochemical reaction and oxide formation (specifically CuO). The text does not explain why this specific temperature was selected or provide phase stability boundaries.
answers.conditions: Wear test at 300 °C against alloy steel
answers.measurement_outcome: High COF, wear rate 1.5 (relative units), formation of CuO
answers.mechanism: High COF at 300 °C relates to tribochemical reaction and oxide formation
answers.boundary_limitation: No explanation for temperature selection; no phase stability limits reported.
evidence_spans: The deposited high-entropy films were annealed at 300, 400, and 500 °C to increase the adhesion of the film to the 304 stainless-steel substrate.
The annealed CuMoTaWV film at 300 °C ( Figure 10 a) showed the lowest surface roughnesses of 2 nm (Sa) and 3 nm (Sq).

Based on these findings, the RHEA film annealed at 300 °C showed the lowest surface roughness ( Figure 10 d) and was thus chosen to study the tribological behavior and compared with the as-deposited film.
